chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: Other musicians' Muslim names; his son born a Muslim
summary: He did not announce his faith when others took names like Sahib Shihab, and took his first son, born in Paris in 1950, to the mosque.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: So I've always felt -- I've seen, like some guys who converted, their names were like Shihab, his name
Well, we all came up playing with Tadd and all of them.

So one day I said, 'Hey, Edmund.' 'Don't call me Edmund.' I said, 'Oh, wait a minute. What are you talking about?' He said, 'My Muslim name is Sahib Shihab.' I said, 'Okay, okay, okay.' But you know, I was a Muslim.
And I wouldn't let anyone know.
When my son was born, my first son was born here in 1950 in Paris, and I took him, the first thing I did, when he got old enough, he was about four or five months old --
-- old enough for me to take out and carry around, --
-- I took him to the mosque. And the [Imman] prayed over him and so forth, and he was born a Muslim.
He had to have a blessing.
I said, well he's not going to be a convert. He's going to be born one.
So whether he believes or whether he adheres to the religion --
He's got that gift at birth.
That's right. He's born a Muslim.
